## About this notebook

This notebook queries the registry bundle, one RDF graph over several static Wikibase instances, with SPARQL in the browser. Nothing is sent to a server.

The roles `bbr:instanceOf`, `bbr:subclassOf`, `bbr:partOf` and the others are the same in every instance, although
the Wikibase properties behind them are not (`P1` and `P2` are swapped between fuzzy-sl and chublets). Ask across
instances through the roles.


## Step 1: set up and load the graph

`rdflib` is not bundled with Pyodide, so it is installed with `micropip`. HTTP has to go through
`pyodide.http.pyfetch`: `requests` and `urllib.request` do not work in the browser.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
#| label: setup
#| output: false
import micropip
await micropip.install("rdflib==7.1.1")

from pyodide.http import pyfetch
from rdflib import Graph

GRAPH_URL = "https://beaverbridge-framework.github.io/beaverbridge-registry/downloads/beaverbridge-registry.ttl"

PREFIXES = """
PREFIX bbr: <https://beaverbridge-framework.github.io/beaverbridge-registry/vocab/>
PREFIX dcat: <http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#>
PREFIX dct: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX wikibase: <http://wikiba.se/ontology#>
"""

async def load(url):
    resp = await pyfetch(url)
    if resp.status != 200:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{url} -> HTTP {resp.status}")
    g = Graph()
    g.parse(data=await resp.string(), format="turtle")
    return g

def show(graph, query):
    """Run a query and return the rows as a list of dicts."""
    res = graph.query(PREFIXES + query)
    cols = [str(v) for v in res.vars]
    return [{c: (None if r[i] is None else str(r[i])) for i, c in enumerate(cols)} for r in res]
```

The bundle is about 0.9 MB.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
#| label: load-graph
base = await load(GRAPH_URL)
print(f"{len(base)} triples loaded from {GRAPH_URL}")
```

## Step 2: Which instances are in the registry?

One catalogue record per instance: where it comes from, under which licence, written by which version of wikibase-static, and how large the export was before the registry kept what a search needs.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
#| label: query-instances
assert "base" in dir(), "Run the 'load-graph' cell first."
rows = show(base, """
SELECT ?instance ?title ?licence ?generator ?dataAsOf ?sourceTriples WHERE {
  ?record a dcat:CatalogRecord ;
          bbr:prefix ?instance ;
          dct:title ?title ;
          bbr:sourceTripleCount ?sourceTriples .
  OPTIONAL { ?record bbr:generator ?generator }
  OPTIONAL { ?record dct:modified ?dataAsOf }
  OPTIONAL { ?record foaf:primaryTopic/dct:license ?licence }
}
ORDER BY ?instance""")

for r in rows:
    print(" | ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in r.items() if v is not None))
print(f"\n{len(rows)} rows")
```
## Step 3: Which classes have how many items?

The same question in every instance, asked through <code>bbr:instanceOf</code>. The English label of the class is shown; some classes have a second label in another language.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
#| label: query-classes
assert "base" in dir(), "Run the 'load-graph' cell first."
rows = show(base, """
SELECT ?instance ?class (COUNT(DISTINCT ?item) AS ?items) WHERE {
  ?item bbr:instanceOf ?c ;
        bbr:fromInstance/bbr:prefix ?instance .
  ?c rdfs:label ?class .
  FILTER(LANG(?class) = "en")
}
GROUP BY ?instance ?class
ORDER BY ?instance DESC(?items) ?class""")

for r in rows:
    print(" | ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in r.items() if v is not None))
print(f"\n{len(rows)} rows")
```
## Step 4: How are the classes related?

Subclass links of all instances, through <code>bbr:subclassOf</code>. Each row is one link from a class to its superclass.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
#| label: query-hierarchy
assert "base" in dir(), "Run the 'load-graph' cell first."
rows = show(base, """
SELECT ?instance ?class ?superclass WHERE {
  ?c bbr:subclassOf ?s ;
     bbr:fromInstance/bbr:prefix ?instance ;
     rdfs:label ?class .
  ?s rdfs:label ?superclass .
  FILTER(LANG(?class) = "en" && LANG(?superclass) = "en")
}
ORDER BY ?instance ?superclass ?class""")

for r in rows:
    print(" | ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in r.items() if v is not None))
print(f"\n{len(rows)} rows")
```
## Step 5: Which Wikibase property stands behind a role?

The registry writes every role as a normalised statement next to the source statement. Asking for the source predicate that carries the same object shows the crosswalk at work: <em>instance of</em> is <code>P1</code> in one instance and <code>P2</code> in the other.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
#| label: query-roles
assert "base" in dir(), "Run the 'load-graph' cell first."
rows = show(base, """
SELECT DISTINCT ?instance (REPLACE(STR(?role), "^.*/", "bbr:") AS ?roleName) ?sourcePredicate WHERE {
  VALUES ?role { bbr:instanceOf bbr:subclassOf bbr:partOf bbr:externalMatch }
  ?s ?role ?o ;
     bbr:fromInstance/bbr:prefix ?instance ;
     ?sourcePredicate ?o .
  FILTER(?sourcePredicate != ?role)
}
ORDER BY ?roleName ?instance""")

for r in rows:
    print(" | ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in r.items() if v is not None))
print(f"\n{len(rows)} rows")
```
## Step 6: Which classes state a CIDOC CRM class?

Only classes that carry an equivalent class IRI themselves are listed. A class without a row here has no anchor in its own instance.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
#| label: query-crm-anchors
assert "base" in dir(), "Run the 'load-graph' cell first."
rows = show(base, """
SELECT ?instance ?class ?crm WHERE {
  ?c bbr:equivalentClass ?crm ;
     bbr:fromInstance/bbr:prefix ?instance ;
     rdfs:label ?class .
  FILTER(LANG(?class) = "en")
}
ORDER BY ?instance ?class""")

for r in rows:
    print(" | ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in r.items() if v is not None))
print(f"\n{len(rows)} rows")
```
## Step 7: Which items have coordinates?

Items with a position, as the source states it (WKT, longitude first). Only instances with a coordinate property show up.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
#| label: query-coordinates
assert "base" in dir(), "Run the 'load-graph' cell first."
rows = show(base, """
SELECT ?instance ?item ?class ?coordinates WHERE {
  ?i bbr:coordinates ?coordinates ;
     bbr:fromInstance/bbr:prefix ?instance ;
     rdfs:label ?item .
  FILTER(LANG(?item) = "en")
  OPTIONAL {
    ?i bbr:instanceOf ?c .
    ?c rdfs:label ?class .
    FILTER(LANG(?class) = "en")
  }
}
ORDER BY ?instance ?item""")

for r in rows:
    print(" | ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in r.items() if v is not None))
print(f"\n{len(rows)} rows")
```
## Step 8: Which items point to Wikidata?

Plain Q-numbers in the sources are turned into Wikidata IRIs by the bundle step, so this works the same for every instance.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
#| label: query-wikidata
assert "base" in dir(), "Run the 'load-graph' cell first."
rows = show(base, """
SELECT ?instance ?item ?wikidata WHERE {
  ?i bbr:wikidataEquivalent ?wikidata ;
     bbr:fromInstance/bbr:prefix ?instance ;
     rdfs:label ?item .
  FILTER(LANG(?item) = "en")
}
ORDER BY ?instance ?item""")

for r in rows:
    print(" | ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in r.items() if v is not None))
print(f"\n{len(rows)} rows")
```
## Step 9: Where do the external matches lead?

Matches are grouped by the host of the URL they point to.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
#| label: query-match-hosts
assert "base" in dir(), "Run the 'load-graph' cell first."
rows = show(base, """
SELECT ?instance ?host (COUNT(?i) AS ?links) WHERE {
  ?i bbr:externalMatch ?url ;
     bbr:fromInstance/bbr:prefix ?instance .
  BIND(REPLACE(STR(?url), "^https?://([^/]+).*$", "$1") AS ?host)
}
GROUP BY ?instance ?host
ORDER BY DESC(?links) ?host""")

for r in rows:
    print(" | ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in r.items() if v is not None))
print(f"\n{len(rows)} rows")
```
## Step 10: Which properties does each instance define?

All properties with their datatype. The numbers are local to the instance; the label and datatype are what can be compared.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
#| label: query-properties
assert "base" in dir(), "Run the 'load-graph' cell first."
rows = show(base, """
SELECT ?instance ?property ?label ?datatype WHERE {
  ?p a wikibase:Property ;
     rdfs:label ?label ;
     wikibase:propertyType ?t ;
     bbr:fromInstance/bbr:prefix ?instance .
  FILTER(LANG(?label) = "en")
  BIND(REPLACE(STR(?p), "^.*/", "") AS ?property)
  BIND(REPLACE(STR(?t), "^.*#", "") AS ?datatype)
}
ORDER BY ?instance ?datatype ?label""")

for r in rows:
    print(" | ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in r.items() if v is not None))
print(f"\n{len(rows)} rows")
```
## Step 11: Which labels occur in more than one instance?

Equal names are reported and never merged: the registry only states that two entries share a label, not that they are the same thing. Whether <em>Florian Thiery</em> in both instances is one person is for a person to say.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
#| label: query-same-label
assert "base" in dir(), "Run the 'load-graph' cell first."
rows = show(base, """
SELECT ?label ?a ?x ?b ?y WHERE {
  ?x rdfs:label ?label ;
     bbr:fromInstance/bbr:prefix ?a .
  ?y rdfs:label ?label ;
     bbr:fromInstance/bbr:prefix ?b .
  FILTER(?a < ?b && LANG(?label) = "en")
}
ORDER BY ?label""")

for r in rows:
    print(" | ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in r.items() if v is not None))
print(f"\n{len(rows)} rows")
```

---

Produced by `beaverbridge-registry`, the prototype of BeaverBridge. Vocabulary: `metadata/bbr.ttl`.
